newsitem.title: USA: LIPA says tax break key to BU, LILCO pact.
newsitem.headline: LIPA says tax break key to BU, LILCO pact.

text.p: Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) said Wednesday a waiver on federal capital gains taxes would be key to the success of its plans to buy utility assets from Brooklyn Union Gas and Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO).
"An adverse ruling from the IRS (Internal Revenue Service) would cripple this solution," said LIPA chairman Frank Zarb at a news conference in Uniondale, N.Y., referring to the proposed deal.

Zarb explained that if the IRS turned down the state agency's request, other options could be explored, including a "pre-packaged condemnation" of the Shoreham nuclear power plant or some form of securitization. He did not elaborate.
"We're not without a fallback position," he said.
Zarb added that the agency is facing a June deadline for submitting all its paperwork to the IRS, a process it already has started.
LIPA looks for the IRS to hand down its ruling fairly swiftly.
"It certainly should be this year. We're hopeful no later than the third quarter," Zarb said.

The huge transaction, which includes one of the country's largest-ever tax-free bond sales, requires a raft of regulatory approvals, including the Public Authorities Control Borad, New York State Public Service Commission, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Zarb said he hoped the deal would be approved as early as late 1997 or early 1998.

Details of the agreement, announced earlier Wednesday, includes LIPA's purchase of LILCO's power lines and its share in the Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear power plant from a holding company being jointly created by LILCO and Brooklyn Union.

New York Governor George Pataki said the pact would eventually lower Long Island's electricity rates by 20 percent over the next five years. Long Islanders currently pay some of the nations' highest electricity prices.
